axes: Roblox: X east, Y up, Z south (glTF +Y up; Blender (x,y,z) -> Roblox (x,z,-y))

assets.name: M1_Horn
assets.notes: 3 pairs of sails round a hollow walk-in core (base corners 21 from the axis, apex 44 over the deck); mouths (A-frames 16 tall, 14 wide) at 60/180/300 in dark frames 19 wide at the deck; at each star point (0/120/240) one broad folded sail (tip 48 up and 14 out, ridge sweeping down to the deck 38 out, sealed to the walls up to 16) and behind it a thin fin 53 tall. Colouring (b): the trailer's: pale blue-teal sails, navy mouth frames, cobalt inside, gold trim. Inside: cobalt panels, gold fans, weapon racks and supply bags (props, not loot). Pivot: deck centre (world y 52).
assets.pivot: base centre on the ground (see notes)
assets.collisionNote: the walls collide through M1_Horn_HornCollide: six closed convex slabs inside the walls (invisible: set Transparency 1, CastShadow false). The wall faces, the panels, the racks and the trim do not collide. The sails and fins collide as modelled (closed shells). The floor is HornFloor (a slab, Box).
assets.colouringsNote: both colourings share this mesh: to switch, set these parts' colours (the HornRack's second colour group is the gold too)

notes: One flat colour per part: rgb (sRGB) is the part's painted tone (UpcomingFilm_Brief 1.10) and is also the base colour of the part's material in the GLB (one material per role and colour). A part painted in several colours is exported as its colour groups: <asset>_<role>, <asset>_<role>_2, ... (colourGroup n of colourGroups), all with the role's Roblox material and collision. The GLB carries no vertex colours and no textures: the +-3-6% facet value jitter and the top/underside shading seen in the Blender previews are NOT in the export (a later baked colour map, ArtStyle rule 4-5, carries them). Every part is single-sided; 'faces' says which way an open sheet was turned (up, out from or in toward the asset's vertical axis).
